title: Eight amazing places to visit around the world

vocab.articleQuote: See 7,000 years of ancient history, all in one place.
vocab.meaning: Ancient means very, very old. It is used for things from a super long time ago, long before your grandparents were born. In the article, ancient history means the story of people who lived thousands of years ago.
examples: We saw an ancient tree that is older than our whole town.
The museum has ancient pots that people made a very long time ago.

vocab.articleQuote: They depict animals that are extinct, or no longer exist.
vocab.meaning: When a kind of animal is extinct, there are none left alive anywhere. They are gone for good. In the article, the rock carvings show animals that are extinct, so nobody can see them alive today.
examples: Dinosaurs are extinct, so we can only see their bones in a museum.
My book has a picture of a big, hairy elephant that is now extinct.

vocab.articleQuote: They’ve been preserved, so you can get up close.
vocab.meaning: If something is preserved, it has been kept safe so it does not change or fall apart. People can look at it for a very long time. In the article, the animals at the museum have been preserved, so visitors can see them up close.
examples: Grandma preserved my baby shoes in a box, and they still look new.
We preserved a pretty leaf by pressing it flat inside a heavy book.

concepts.name: Pharaoh
concepts.articleQuote: It has every item found in King Tut’s tomb.
concepts.meaning:
The article tells about King Tut. He was a pharaoh. A pharaoh was the king of ancient Egypt. That was a land beside the Nile River, more than 3,000 years ago.

A pharaoh was a bit like a king in a storybook. He was the leader of the whole land. People thought he was very special. When a pharaoh died, his family put him in a tomb, which is a special place made just for him. They filled it with treasures, like gold and fancy furniture.

The pharaohs also had the giant pyramids built. The Pyramids of Giza, near the museum in the article, are some of them. Each pyramid was built to hold a pharaoh.

So a pharaoh was the king of ancient Egypt, and his treasures help us learn how people lived long ago.

quiz.question: What can you see at the Grand Egyptian Museum?
options: Every item found in King Tut’s tomb
quiz.explanation: The museum has every item found in King Tut’s tomb. The Pyramids of Giza are nearby.

quiz.question: Who makes the waves at Surf Abu Dhabi?
quiz.explanation: The waves at Surf Abu Dhabi are made by a machine. It is the world’s biggest wave pool.

quiz.question: What is special about the Art Zoo Museum in Amsterdam?
options: It has a glass floor high in the sky
It has a pool for surfers
It is full of animals that died long ago and were preserved
It lets you swim with fish
quiz.explanation: The Art Zoo Museum is not a real zoo. It is full of creatures that have been preserved, so you can see them up close.

quiz.question: The rock carvings in Australia show animals that are extinct. What does extinct mean?
quiz.explanation: Extinct means there are no more of that kind of animal alive anywhere.

quiz.question: What was a pharaoh?
quiz.explanation: A pharaoh was the king of ancient Egypt. King Tut was one.
